diagnosis.original_evidence: R84 SelectSpriteQueueNode increments SpriteQueueNodeEpoch on every selection, including when a native node pointer is selected again; the stage D3DX transition helper gated on outgoingNode != incomingNode.
source_trace: Original 0x00498670 calls one of six exact sprite/numeric E8s with StageExtensionTime producer ownership.
Native D3DX Draw can defer GPU execution past source return and does not necessarily flush on a SpriteNode reselection.
BeforeQueueNode calls CanIsolateD3DXStageQueueNodeTransition before changing queued node/epoch; old helper skipped the same-pointer case.
Patched helper treats any new valid StageExtensionTime selection as physical epoch boundary while retaining the existing homogeneous/outgoing-owner/native Flush proof.
alternatives_rejected: No global D3DX per-Draw Flush, no SkyGlow/HUD generic retag, no synthetic game timer changes, no bypass of physical R84/host stereo admission.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: A reused node pointer has a new R84 queue epoch after SelectSpriteQueueNode; the previous queued D3DX triangles must be submitted with the OLD epoch before R30/R33 evaluates the next eye. Actual Quest3 optical outcome is still untested.
diagnosis.root_cause: Queue-boundary admission compared only SpriteNode pointer inequality, despite physical draw identity requiring both pointer and incremented queue epoch.
